facts.text: Wheelchair-accessible seats with companion seats are in the Lower Gallery and Upper Gallery and can be booked online or by calling the Box Office.
facts.quote: We have wheelchair accessible seats, along with companion seats, available in the Lower Gallery and Upper Gallery. These can be booked online or by calling the Box Office.

facts.text: A wheelchair-accessible ramp in the first-floor Linnemann Family Lobby leads to the left-hand theatre doors; the Upper Gallery center section is on one level and reached by an elevator in the lobby.
facts.quote: A wheelchair-accessible ramp is located in the Linnemann Family Lobby of the first floor, leading up to the left-hand doors of the theatre. The Upper Gallery center section is all on the same level and can be access via elevator in the lobby.

facts.text: Free assisted listening devices are offered at all performances, picked up at the Box Office on arrival; they include a DSP loop driver for T-coil-equipped hearing aids.
facts.quote: We offer assisted listening devices at all performances. These are complimentary and can be picked up from the Box Office upon arrival. These amplify the sound heard from the stage and can pair with your hearing aids or can be used with your earphones. The devices include a DSP loop driver for anyone using a T-coil-equipped hearing aid.

facts.text: Each production has live sign language interpreted performances and at least one live audio-described performance, typically at the final matinee; advance reservations for audio description are appreciated.
quote: For Patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing, Sign Language interpreted performances are offered during the run of each production by live interpreters from the stage. These are typically scheduled for the final matinee performance.

For Patrons who are blind or have low vision, we offer at least one audio-described performance per production. This service is provided by a live person who will be describing the non-spoken action of the performance. Advance reservations are appreciated. Patrons utilizing this resource can pick up a headset from the Box Office on the scheduled night. These are typically scheduled for the final matinee performance.

facts.text: Sensory-friendly performances are modified for people with autism or developmental or sensory differences, with front-of-house staff and volunteers trained for them.
facts.quote: These special performances are uniquely adapted for individuals with autism and/or those with developmental and/or sensory differences to enjoy with their families. The performances are modified and front-of-house staff and volunteers are trained to facilitate a safe, judgement-free environment.

facts.text: The seating page lists three wheelchair positions (two Lower Gallery, one Upper), but also says removable Upper Gallery seats can accommodate additional wheelchairs; arrange this with the Box Office at 513-381-2273. Entry from the lobby is at Row D, with no steps to Row D seats. Floor seating added on the lowered stage requires one step down.
quote: There are 3 Wheelchair accessible seats- 2 in the Lower Gallery and 1 in the Upper Gallery*.
All of the seats in the Upper Gallery are loose and removable so many wheelchairs could be accommodated at one time. Reach out to our Box Office at 513-381-2273 to plan your visit.
You will enter the theater at Row D on each side so the level is flat and there are no steps required to reach any seat in Row D.
When we lower the stage, we will be adding "Floor Seating". These seats are all on one level and can only be reached by going down 1 step.

facts.text: Transfer-arm seats are available and marked on the seating chart.
facts.quote: There are also transfer arm seats available and they are noted on the seating chart.

facts.text: All-gender restrooms on the second floor are individual locking stalls with a shared sink.
facts.quote: All-gender restrooms are located on the second floor. These restrooms are individual stalls with locks and a shared sink.

facts.text: Sensory-friendly shows reduce lighting and sound effects, and audience members may leave and return for breaks as often as needed.
quote: Intensity of lighting and sound effects reduced during performance.
The performance will be approx 2 hours with an intermission but audiences members may come and go in and out of the theater space for breaks as often as needed.

facts.text: The Washington Park garage needs no phone, and an attendant is usually available to help.
facts.quote: You receive a ticket on entry and then pay at payment stations on your way back to your car—no mobile phone is required, and an attendant is usually available to assist.

facts.text: In the Upper Gallery, the center three sections do not require stairs, but the two side sections have a step down. Arrange the exact seat location with the Box Office rather than assuming every Upper Gallery seat is on the elevator level.
facts.quote: In the Upper Galley, the center 3 sections also do not require stairs. The side 2 sections have a step down to reach them.

facts.text: The seating page gives seat widths of 21–23 inches and directs visitors to its floor-plan schematic for individual seat numbers, widths and stairs. These are publisher specifications, not Threshold measurements.
facts.quote: The seats range from 21" to 23" inches wide. For a detailed schematic map of the seats and widths (including seat numbers and stairs) see the "Floor Plan" tab above.

facts.text: For the advertised sensory-friendly performances, house lights remain at 50% and the venue states a sound cap of 90 decibels. These are performance adjustments, not a guarantee of quiet or suitability for a particular visitor.
quote: House lights will remain dimmed at 50% during performance.
Sound will be capped at 90 decibels.

facts.text: The sensory-friendly performance page promises two break areas, on the first and second levels, plus headphones and fidgets during the show. Confirm the arrangements for your performance; this page does not describe an everyday staffed quiet room.
quote: Two break areas will be provided, on the first and second levels.
Headphones and fidgets will be provided during the show.

facts.text: For sensory-friendly performances, the venue says attendance is limited to half its standard capacity and the front two rows are intentionally left unavailable.
facts.quote: The house will be monitored and limited to half-capacity of our standard performances. The front two rows closest to the stage will also be intentionally blocked off.

facts.text: The sensory-friendly page says closed captioning and audio description can be arranged with advance requests. It does not state a request deadline; confirm the service for the chosen performance.
facts.quote: Closed captioning and audio descriptions can be made available upon advanced request.

facts.text: The parking page describes the Towne Center option at 1251 Central Parkway as a surface lot paid entirely by phone, using a text message or posted code. It says there is no attended or in-person payment option there; policies and availability may change.
quote: Situated at 1251 Central Parkway, Cincinnati, OH 45202, this surface lot is a convenient alternative with ample spaces.
Payment here is handled entirely via mobile phone—you’ll need to text or scan the posted codes, as this lot does not offer attended or in person payment options.
Policies, rates, and availability are subject to change without notice.

facts.text: The sensory pre-visit narrative places the elevator to the second floor down the hallway to the right of the Box Office. Confirm the current route and elevator operation with the venue.
facts.quote: I can also access the second floor by accessing the elevator. The elevator is down the hallway located on the right side of the Box Office.

facts.text: The sensory pre-visit narrative places first-floor restrooms along the hallway to the right of the Box Office: men’s at the second door on the left and women’s at the third. Its photos show the approaches, not cubicle dimensions or adult-changing equipment; confirm current arrangements.
quote: There are restrooms on the first floor down the hallway that is on the right side of the Box Office.
In the hallway, the men’s restroom is the second door on the left.
In the hallway, the women’s restroom is the third door on the left.

facts.text: Entrances and exits have ramps; the first entrance has an automatic door. Main exhibits use gradual ramps, with an elevator back to the main level.
quote: Ramps are located at every entrance and exit door to the Creation Museum. The first entrance features an automatic door.

A series of gradual ramps take visitors through the Creation Museum’s main exhibits. This one-way path passes through all of the Walk-Through Biblical History and ends on the lower level, where you can bring an elevator back to the main level.

facts.text: The museum identifies Dino Den as an exception to wheelchair exhibit access. Guest Services offers wheelchairs first come, first served; the page describes electric mobility vehicles as limited in number.
quote: Virtually every exhibit (except the "Dino Den") is wheelchair accessible.
You may bring your own, or Guest Services offers both strollers and wheelchairs for the convenience of all visitors on a first-come, first-served basis.
A limited number of Electric Convenience Vehicles (ECVs) are available for a $45 fee.

facts.text: Complimentary sensory kits, noise-reducing earmuffs and earplugs are available at the Welcome Center and Guest Services. The 4D theater shows use strobe and flashing lights (the museum warns guests with photosensitive epilepsy), loud audio, shaking seats and puffs of air. The first Corruption exhibit also has mild flashing lights and sounds of war and pain; it can be passed through quickly.
quote: For guests with sensory sensitivities, complimentary sensory kits, as well as noise-reducing earmuffs and earplugs, are available and can be accessed at the Welcome Center upon arrival and the Guest Services desk inside the Main Hall of the museum.
The shows include 4D effects such as rumbling and shaking seats, loud audio, and puffs of air.
Additionally, strobe lights are used in these presentations.
contain a sequence of flashing lights that may affect guests who are susceptible to photosensitive epilepsy or other photo sensitivities.

Additionally, the first Corruption exhibit, halfway through the main exhibits, includes mild flashing lights, flashing pictures on the walls, and various sounds of war and pain—all depicting the brokenness of this world after sin entered. This exhibit can be passed through quickly if needed.

facts.text: A photo social story and accessibility map help visitors prepare.
quote: Learn more about visiting the Creation Museum by watching our social story
Please also reference our Accessibility Map on the Museum Maps Page for additional helpful information.

Read our Social Story that features 22 photos that walk you through the various locations at the Creation Museum and provide helpful information to prepare you for sensory and accessibility accommodations.

facts.text: The museum lists vegetarian and gluten-free dining options and asks visitors to consult a restaurant manager about dietary needs.
quote: We offer both vegetarian and gluten-free options at Sprig & Stone Casual Dining.
And if you have any questions regarding dietary needs during your visit, please request to speak with a restaurant manager—we would be glad to assist you!

facts.text: Guest Services offers manual wheelchair rentals for $15 and a limited number of ECVs for $45 on arrival. Rental fees are non-refundable. Confirm equipment availability before relying on a rental.
quote: Manual wheelchairs are available for a $15 fee.
A limited number of Electric Convenience Vehicles (ECVs) are available for a $45 fee. ECVs are available from Guest Services on arrival at the Creation Museum.
Rental fees are non-refundable.
Guest Services offers both strollers and wheelchairs for the convenience of all visitors on a first-come, first-served basis.

facts.text: The museum describes all its theaters as accessible and lists wheelchair locations and companion seats in the Special Effects Theater and Planetarium. Ask a theater attendant about reserving those spaces.
facts.quote: All theaters are accessible—the Special Effects Theater and the Planetarium include wheelchair locations and companion seats. See a theater attendant for more information about reserving these spaces.

facts.text: The museum describes restrooms throughout its facility and grounds as accessible and locates wheelchair-accessible drinking fountains near the main interior restrooms; it does not give fixture dimensions. Its accessibility page also says visitors may reenter the exhibits at any time.
quote: All restrooms throughout the facility and grounds are accessible. Wheelchair accessible water fountains are also available near the main interior restrooms.
Reentrance to the exhibits can be done at any time during your visit.

facts.text: Planetarium shows have closed captioning on request (ask when buying tickets), and a descriptive audio tour of the main exhibits plays on your own device.
quote: Closed captioning is available upon request for all Stargazer Planetarium shows. Simply ask when purchasing Planetarium tickets.
The Creation Museum is pleased to offer a descriptive audio tour for the main exhibits. Guests can listen on their own devices.

facts.text: The accessibility page describes a paved, mile-long Botanical Gardens trail with five bridges and a boardwalk, and directs visitors to its accessibility map for bridge access. This description does not establish that every bridge is step-free.
facts.quote: The Botanical Gardens feature a paved nature trail that is a mile in length including five bridges and a boardwalk. Please reference the Accessibility Map for more information on bridge accessibility.

facts.text: The museum lists designated accessible spaces in its main parking lot and asks visitors who need help finding an available space to alert the person directing traffic.
facts.quote: We have many accessible parking spaces available in our main parking lot. If you need assistance finding an available space, alert the individual directing traffic.

facts.text: For adult changing-table information, the museum directs visitors to Guest Services inside the museum. This page does not identify a table location, transfer equipment, dimensions or availability.
facts.quote: For more information on adult changing tables, please talk to a team member at the Guest Services desk inside the Creation Museum.

facts.text: The zoo’s center interactive pen has a sand surface. The museum says the other pens can be viewed from paved trails; this does not establish entry to every pen.
facts.quote: With the exception of the center interactive pen (which has a sand surface), all of the zoo’s pens are fully viewable via paved trails.

facts.text: To borrow the complimentary sensory kits, earmuffs or earplugs, visitors give their name and phone number to the museum team. Reservations are not needed, and items are returned to Guest Services before departure.
quote: For guests with sensory sensitivities, complimentary sensory kits, as well as noise-reducing earmuffs and earplugs, are available and can be accessed at the Welcome Center upon arrival and the Guest Services desk inside the Main Hall of the museum.
Simply provide the museum team with your name and phone number to utilize these options during your visit. All items can be returned to the Guest Services Desk before your departure.
(Note: Reservation of these options is not necessary.)

facts.text: The break exit at the start of the Corruption exhibits, just after Garden of Eden, is a stairwell back to the first level. The accessibility page does not identify a step-free break route at that point; ask staff before relying on this exit.
facts.quote: Take a break at any time from the exhibits via an emergency exit (a stairwell back to the first level) located on the right where the Corruption exhibits begin and just after the Garden of Eden ends.

facts.text: A two-way door beside the Lucy hologram in Starting Points bypasses the Biblical Authority room. A separate bypass on the right in the Christ, Cross and Consummation area avoids Legacy Hall crowds and leads to Borderlands.
quote: This option is a two-way door located directly beside the Lucy hologram in the Starting Points room.
There are also shortcuts throughout the main exhibits, including one early on to bypass the Biblical Authority room if it is congested.
Additionally, there is a bypass on the right in the Christ, Cross, and Consummation area to avoid the Legacy Hall auditorium crowds. This bypass will take you to the next exhibit called Borderlands

facts.text: The museum says restroom and elevator signs include Braille.
facts.quote: Restrooms and elevators are marked in Braille to assist with finding your way in the museum.

facts.text: Closed captioning for The Last Adam is available on request, and captioning devices are available at the 4D Theater. Ask staff about the device and show arrangements.
facts.quote: Closed captioning is also available upon request for The Last Adam show, and there are closed captioning devices available at the 4D Theater as well.

facts.text: The entrance theater can be crowded and loud; its roughly one-minute video may be skipped or revisited. Starting Points has several videos playing around the room, which the museum describes as substantial audio stimulation.
quote: Immediately upon entrance to the main exhibits, there is a theater that can be crowded and includes loud audio. The video that plays is about one minute long and can be skipped or simply returned to later.
Starting Points is the next room, and various video displays play on the walls. Please note that there is substantial audio stimulation in this room from the different videos playing around you.

facts.text: The tactile-experience request page welcomes guests with low vision, blindness or autism, together with their immediate family or assistant. It asks for requests at least two weeks before the visit and lists sessions Monday–Saturday at 2 p.m.; confirm availability against seasonal museum opening days.
quote: We are so pleased to offer the Creation Museum tactile experience to our guests who have low vision, are blind, or are on the autism spectrum. The immediate family or assistant of the individual requesting this experience is welcome to attend.
Guest Services staff offer the tactile experience Monday–Saturday at 2:00 p.m.
Please submit your request below at least two weeks before your visit to ensure the availability of this unique, complimentary experience!

facts.text: The published October 25, 2026–January 2, 2027 schedule opens Monday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., and closes Sundays, Thanksgiving Day (November 26) and Christmas Eve/Day (December 24–25). Holiday evening programs have separate dates and hours.
quote: October 25, 2026–January 2, 2027* Monday to Saturday 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Sunday Closed
*Closed Thanksgiving Day, November 26, 2026.
*Closed Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, December 24–25, 2026.
Christmas Program Hours Celebrate Christmas on select nights during our free holiday-exclusive event, Christmas at the Creation Museum

facts.text: For January 3–March 6, 2027, the posted museum schedule is Wednesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., with Sunday–Tuesday closures. Confirm operating days before booking travel or an accommodation.
facts.quote: January 3, 2027–March 6, 2027 Wednesday to Saturday 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Sunday to Tuesday Closed

facts.text: Parking booths open 30 minutes before the museum. The hours page states that last admission is one hour before closing and that all times are Eastern; operating hours may change.
quote: Parking booths open 30 minutes before the Creation Museum.
All hours are Eastern Time.
Last admission is one hour before closing. Operating hours are subject to change.

facts.text: The museum’s service-animal policy asks visitors accompanied by an animal to contact public safety or another staff member on arrival. Except for emergencies or public-safety necessity, staff cannot take control of service animals; guests remain responsible for control and cleanup.
quote: Individuals entering the premises who are accompanied by an animal should contact public safety or another staff member upon their arrival.

Except in the event of an emergency or when otherwise necessary in the interest of public safety, employees of AiG and the Creation Museum are not permitted to take control of service animals at any time. Guests are responsible for the cleanup and for controlling their service animal’s behavior.

facts.text: Wheelchair-accessible seats and companion seats are offered at all price levels, with additional wheelchair-transfer seating in the Orchestra and Dress Circle. The Emery Theater has an elevator; email the theater to request an accessible seat.
quote: We are excited to provide wheelchair accessible seats and companion seats in all price levels at the Emery Theater.
There are additional options for wheelchair-transfer seating in our Orchestra and Dress Circle sections of the theater, viewable with information overlays during ticket selection.
Please email us if you need a wheelchair accessible seat. Please note: There IS an elevator at the Emery Theater.

facts.text: Selected MainStage performances have an ASL interpreter standing at audience left, and audio description is offered at the second Saturday 2 p.m. performance of each 2026–27 MainStage production.
quote: we provide an experienced theatre interpreter who stands to the audience left side of the Emery Theater stage and translates what the actors are saying or singing into American Sign Language (ASL).
TCT will offer audio description services during the second Saturday 2:00 PM performances of all MainStage productions in the 2026–2027 season at the Emery Theater.

facts.text: Assistive listening devices can be requested from the Box Office at every TCT performance at the Emery. Limited sensory bags with sunglasses, fidgets and headphones are available there on request at MainStage performances.
quote: Available upon request from the Box Office, every TCT performance at the Emery Theater has the option of an Assistive Listening Device to increase the sound of the show.

A limited number of Sensory-Friendly bags (including sunglasses, fidgets, and headphones) are available upon request at all of our MainStage performances. Just visit the Emery Theater Box Office when you come for a show.

facts.text: A shared quiet space with muted sound, dim lighting and room to move still has a view of the show. Sensory-friendly performances use softer lights and gentler sounds, with no fog or strobes, and have a quiet area.
quote: The room offers muted sound levels, dim lighting and a free movement space while still having a view of the show.
this is a shared space and is not reserved to remain available to all.
Softer lights and gentler sounds make it a cozy experience.
Special effects like fog and strobes? Not this time!
Need a break? Chill out in our Quiet Area staffed with a friendly expert

facts.text: Book a designated wheelchair seat: the theatre may not have a spare wheelchair space to move you to if you buy elsewhere.
facts.quote: We will not necessarily have extra wheelchair accessible seats to move you to if you buy in another location that is not designated wheelchair accessible seating.

facts.text: In its sensory-friendly performance guidance, TCT says a Character Guide, Guide to Attending the Show at Home and downloadable Social Narrative in Word format are available a week before each production. Confirm the resources for the selected show.
facts.quote: Additional resources for the performance, such as a Character Guide, a Guide to Attending the Show at Home, and a downloadable Social Narrative (in Word format) are available a week before each production.

facts.text: Shows usually last under 70 minutes and have no intermission.
quote: Shows typically last less than 70 minutes.
No, all of our shows run without an intermission.

facts.text: If you step out, a monitor on each floor of the Emery shows a live feed of the production.
facts.quote: We’ll also have a live feed of the production on a monitor on each floor of The Emery.

facts.text: Latecomers are seated at an appropriate moment, possibly in the best available seats rather than their reserved ones.
facts.quote: we can’t guarantee that we will be able to seat latecomers in their reserved seat, but we will seat you in the best available seats at an appropriate moment in the performance.

facts.text: The FAQ places the Calming Room at the back of the right side of the first-floor Orchestra section. Visitors may watch some of the performance there before returning to their seats.
facts.quote: In The Emery Theater, we also have a Calming room at the back of the right side of the Orchestra Section on the first floor. Feel free to stop in and watch some of the performance from there before heading back to your seat.

facts.text: Sensory-friendly performances are intended for people with developmental disabilities who may benefit, their classmates and families. TCT says these are not for the general public; all seats require reservation and wheelchair seating is very limited.
quote: These special performances are intended for individuals with developmental disabilities including those on the autism spectrum who may benefit and their classmates and families, not for the general public.
Only a limited number of tickets are sold. All seats are by reservation with very limited wheelchair seating available.

facts.text: For school visits, accessible seating must be requested on the order form and reserved in writing. TCT tries to seat caregivers or age-appropriate students together, but groups with multiple access needs may be split among nearby accessible positions; a request does not guarantee Orchestra seating for the whole group.
quote: Please indicate the number of wheelchair and/or special needs accessible seats you need on the order form. Accessible seating is limited and cannot be guaranteed unless reserved in writing.
We will always do our best to assign students and adult patrons with special needs in seating allowing for a care-giver or other students to be seated with them if they are age appropriate.
For groups including more than one patron with multiple disabilities, they may be separated into various accessible seating locations but as close together as possible.
Requiring special needs seating for select students does not guarantee orchestra floor seating for your entire school group.

facts.text: TCT operates the Emery Box Office beginning one hour before each MainStage performance. The separate Red Bank Road Box Office has different hours; confirm the location before visiting for ticket help.
quote: The Children’s Theatre of Cincinnati operates out of the Emery Theater Box Office beginning 1 hour prior to each of our MainStage performances.
Red Bank Road Box Office: Open Monday-Friday 9 AM to 5 PM

facts.text: The FAQ says weather-related cancellation decisions are made at least two hours before showtime and posted on the website homepage and the theatre’s Facebook and Instagram pages. Check before travelling in hazardous weather.
quote: In the event that hazardous weather or other inclement conditions dictate a decision to cancel a performance, this decision will be made at least two hours prior to show time.
Closure information will be posted on the front page of our website, as well as on our Facebook and Instagram pages.

facts.text: The October 2026 Mary Poppins social narrative places lobby restrooms on the left at the large purple wall. It describes automatic flushing and hand dryers or paper towels. Confirm current fixtures and the route; the guide does not give cubicle dimensions or adult-changing equipment.
quote: If I need to use the restroom, there are restrooms available in the lobby on the left on the big purple wall.
The restrooms flush automatically and have hand dryers or paper towels that I can use to dry my hands.

facts.text: The October 2026 Mary Poppins guide warns that visitors may pass through metal detectors. It describes volunteers with nametags at each door who can answer questions and help visitors find their way. Screening alternatives or assistance procedures are not specified.
quote: We may have to pass through metal detectors first.
At each door, there will be volunteers. They will be wearing special nametags. They will greet us at the door and can help answer questions and show us where to go.

facts.text: Proudworks says its transportation service is available to Northern Kentucky individuals with a valid Kentucky Medicaid card travelling to approved destinations, including employment, day programs and medical appointments. Confirm individual eligibility and the destination with the provider.
facts.quote: Transportation Services are available to individuals in Northern Kentucky with a valid Kentucky Medicaid card traveling to approved destinations, including employment, day programs, and medical appointments.

facts.text: The transportation page says non-emergency medical transport, self-pay and other options may also be available; contact Proudworks for details rather than assuming a particular funding option or trip is approved.
facts.quote: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT), self-pay, and other options may also be available. Contact us for details.

facts.text: The services overview describes travel from home or residential settings to programs and employment sites for Medicaid Waiver consumers in six Northern Kentucky counties. It does not name those counties or describe boarding and transfer assistance.
facts.quote: Proudworks’ Transportation Services provide access from home or residential settings to programs and employment sites for Medicaid Waiver consumers in six counties throughout Northern Kentucky.

facts.text: Proudworks lists community employment, adult day training, social/recreational/respite/day programs, non-emergency medical appointments and community activities among its trip purposes. The transportation page also limits service to approved destinations.
quote: Proudworks provides Transportation services to & from: Community Employment Adult Day Training (ADT) programs-organizations Social, Recreational, Respite, and Day Programs Medical Appointments (Non-Emergency) Community Activities

Transportation Services are available to individuals in Northern Kentucky with a valid Kentucky Medicaid card traveling to approved destinations, including employment, day programs, and medical appointments.

facts.text: For transportation enquiries, the contact page lists Transportation@proudworks.org. Its general contact number is 859-371-4410 and contact hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m.; these are not published ride-service hours.
quote: Get in touch Monday - Friday 8:00AM - 4:00PM 7970 Kentucky Drive, Florence, KY 41042 859-371-4410
Transportation@proudworks.org

facts.text: The distillery’s FAQ describes the whole distillery as one floor without steps. It does not describe the street-to-door connection, doorway controls or restroom layout.
facts.quote: Our distillery is wheelchair friendly, the whole distillery is on one floor without steps making it easy for our friends to navigate our space.

facts.text: Reservations are recommended for tours and tastings because tours can fill. The venue says it will try to fit in callers or walk-ins; this is not a guaranteed place.
facts.quote: Do I need a reservation for a tasting or tour? Reservations are recommended as our tours can fill up but it never hurts to call or show up. We’ll do our best to fit you in.

facts.text: The FAQ describes Thursday tours without lounge coffee or cocktail service, and Friday–Sunday tours and bar service. Confirm your selected date and booking; the Thursday visit is not described as a full lounge visit.
quote: We also offer a midweek tour on Thursdays but our lounge will not be open for coffee and cocktails during that time.
Second Sight Spirits is open on Thursdays for tours and Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays for tour and bar service.

facts.text: Visitors may bring their own food. The FAQ says there is no restaurant, while noting that treats from local companies are brought in; confirm what is available and any ingredient needs directly.
facts.quote: We do not have a restaurant but we do bring in treats from local companies like North South Baking. You are free to bring in your own food as well.

facts.text: The FAQ offers a tasting for visitors who do not have time for a full tour and says guests may wait in the lounge when staff are busy. It does not specify a tasting duration, wait time or seating configuration.
quote: We also offer tastings if you do no have time for a tour.
If we’re busy, feel free to grab a cocktail and relax in our lounge while you wait and we’ll take care of you as soon as we can!

address_quote: Second Sight is located at 301 Elm Street, Ludlow, Kentucky in an old pharmacy.
